meta.title: Operation Glass House: NCII Double Extortion
meta.summary: A sophisticated threat actor has breached a National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII) hub. The crisis evolves from a standard ransomware lockout to a personal, high-stakes psychological war targeting the Board directly.

questions.text: Early monitoring detects anomalous encryption on non-critical back-office servers. Technical teams request a partial 'protective' shutdown of external gateways. What is your strategic directive?
questions.context: A shutdown protects the core but immediately halts public-facing revenue collection and service dashboards.

answers.label: Prioritize Containment: Authorize immediate gateway shutdown
answers.description: Accept service disruption to prevent potential lateral movement into critical control systems.
answers.boardReading: Conservative and safety-first. Minimizes technical risk but creates immediate public visibility.
answers.consequence: Lateral movement is slowed, but media starts asking questions about the 'outage' within minutes.

answers.label: Prioritize Continuity: Maintain services while monitoring
answers.description: Instruct teams to isolate affected servers without a full gateway block to avoid public panic.
answers.boardReading: Aggressive continuity focus. Risks a wider breach for the sake of 'business as usual' appearance.
answers.consequence: Service stays up, but the attacker uses the open gateways to exfiltrate 500GB of sensitive data.

questions.text: The attacker confirms they have exfiltrated unencrypted sensitive data, including customer records and internal Board minutes. They demand $10M or they will leak the data. How do you respond?
questions.context: This is no longer just a technical lockout; it is a data liability and reputational crisis.

answers.label: Engage Law Enforcement and refuse negotiation
answers.description: Maintain a 'No Pay' policy, accelerate data breach notification protocols.
answers.boardReading: Principled and legally defensive. Expects high reputational damage but avoids funding crime.
answers.consequence: The attacker begins leaking small 'proof samples' to dark web forums to increase pressure.

answers.label: Appoint a professional negotiator to stall
answers.description: Open a dialogue to buy time for technical recovery, without promising payment.
answers.boardReading: Tactical. Buys the technical team 24 hours but risks escalating the attacker's aggression.
answers.consequence: The attacker grows impatient and realizes they are being stalled.

questions.text: WILDCARD: Several Board members receive encrypted messages containing current photos of their children and home addresses. The attacker threatens 'physical consequences' if the ransom isn't paid within 4 hours.
questions.context: The crisis has moved from the office to the home. Personal safety is now at stake.

answers.label: Authorize emergency protective security for families
answers.description: Engage private security and police to protect families while maintaining the corporate refusal to pay.
answers.boardReading: Separates personal safety from corporate policy. High cost but preserves integrity.
answers.consequence: The Board remains united but under extreme psychological strain; the attacker prepares a media 'bomb'.

answers.label: Discuss 'Continuity Payment' as a safety measure
answers.description: Consider paying the ransom solely to end the personal threat to family members.
answers.boardReading: Safety-first but high strategic risk. Sets a precedent for future physical extortion.
answers.consequence: The payment is made, but the attacker leaks the data anyway, proving they are unreliable.

questions.text: WILDCARD: A major press outlet receives an anonymous tip-off including the exfiltrated Board minutes and the news of the personal threats. They demand a statement 'coming clean' about the breach scope.
questions.context: The 'Glass House' has shattered. Silence is no longer an option.

answers.label: Full Transparency: Hold a live press conference
answers.description: Acknowledge the breach, the data theft, and the appalling personal threats. State the refusal to be coerced.
answers.boardReading: Radical transparency. Aims to seize the narrative and garner public sympathy against the 'terrorist' tactics.
answers.consequence: Reputational hit is massive, but public trust begins to stabilize as the organization is seen as a victim of extreme crime.

answers.label: Controlled Response: Issue a written legal statement
answers.description: Confirm an 'incident' is under investigation and warn the press about publishing stolen data.
answers.boardReading: Legalistic and protective. Likely to be seen as a cover-up by the public and the press.
answers.consequence: The press publishes the leaked minutes regardless; the organization looks deceptive and out of touch.

questions.text: Technical teams have identified the entry point and prepared a clean rebuild. Government agencies offer to assist in 'offensive' countermeasures against the actor. Do you authorize state intervention?
questions.context: This moves the organization into the realm of national security and international relations.

answers.label: Full State Integration: Hand over all logs and access
answers.description: Allow national security agencies to lead the counter-response and recovery.
answers.boardReading: Responsible NCII governance. Recognizes this as a national threat, not just a corporate one.
answers.consequence: Recovery is slow but secure; the incident is framed as a matter of national resilience.

answers.label: Independent Recovery: Rebuild internally
answers.description: Focus on getting services back up using internal teams to avoid government overreach/scrutiny.
answers.boardReading: Insular. May be faster in the short term but lacks the 'shield' of state protection for future threats.
answers.consequence: Systems come back online, but the underlying actor remains active and poised for a second strike.
